```{r}
#| label: setup
library(reactable)
library(htmltools)

survey <- utils::read.csv("../data-raw/dictionary_survey.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                          encoding = "UTF-8", na.strings = "NA")
survey$model <- ifelse(survey$core, "basic model", "other files")

## A drop-down holding the values of the column, in place of the text filter
select_filter <- function(table_id) {
  function(values, name) {
    tags$select(
      onchange = sprintf("Reactable.setFilter('%s', '%s', event.target.value || undefined)",
                         table_id, name),
      `aria-label` = paste("Filter", name),
      style = "width: 100%;",
      tags$option(value = "", "All"),
      lapply(sort(unique(values)), function(v) tags$option(value = v, v))
    )
  }
}
exact_match <- JS("function(rows, columnId, filterValue) {
  return rows.filter(function(row) { return row.values[columnId] === filterValue })
}")
shown <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "—", x)

## The table of the page, on any subset of the variables
variables_table <- function(data, id) {
  reactable(
    data[, c("variable", "label_long_fr", "label_long_en", "index", "kind", "model")],
    elementId = id,
    searchable = TRUE, filterable = TRUE, highlight = TRUE, compact = TRUE,
    defaultPageSize = 25, showPageSizeOptions = TRUE, pageSizeOptions = c(25, 50, 100, 1000),
    style = list(fontSize = "0.85rem"),
    columns = list(
      variable = colDef(name = "Variable", minWidth = 210,
                        style = list(fontFamily = "monospace", fontWeight = 600)),
      label_long_fr = colDef(name = "Libellé", minWidth = 280, na = "—"),
      label_long_en = colDef(name = "Label", minWidth = 280, na = "—"),
      index = colDef(name = "Index", minWidth = 150,
                     filterInput = select_filter(id), filterMethod = exact_match),
      kind = colDef(name = "Kind", minWidth = 110,
                    filterInput = select_filter(id), filterMethod = exact_match),
      model = colDef(name = "Model", minWidth = 110,
                     filterInput = select_filter(id), filterMethod = exact_match)
    ),
    details = function(i) {
      r <- data[i, ]
      line <- function(what, value) tags$tr(tags$td(style = "padding: 2px 16px 2px 0; color: #666;", what),
                                            tags$td(shown(value)))
      div(style = "padding: 8px 24px 12px 48px; font-size: 0.9em;",
          tags$table(
            line("Short label (fr)", r$label_fr),
            line("Short label (en)", r$label_en),
            line("Forms in the equations", r$index_forms),
            line("Name in the .mdl files", r$mdl_name),
            line("Files", r$files)))
    }
  )
}
```

This page lists the `r nrow(survey)` variables found in the equation files of
ThreeME and in `exogenous.mdl`, with what is known about each. It is built
from `data-raw/dictionary_survey.csv`, itself written by
`data-raw/dictionary_survey.R`.

::: {.callout-note}
## Where the labels come from

The English label of a variable is the `##!` line above the equation that
defines it, unless the dictionary of the package already has one. The French
label is a translation of it, not yet reviewed. A dash means that nothing is
known: `r sum(is.na(survey$label_long_en))` variables have no label, and only
`r sum(!is.na(survey$label_en))` have a short one.
:::

## All variables

Type in the search box to look through every column, or under a column title
to filter that column. Click the arrow at the start of a line for the short
labels, the forms the variable takes in the equations and the files that
define it.

```{r}
#| label: all
#| column: screen-inset
variables_table(survey, "all-variables")
```

## Reading the columns

**Index** says what the variable is indexed by, all forms together: `CID`
exists as `CID`, `CID[c]`, `CID[s]` and `CID[c, s]`, so its index is
`commodity,sector`. The forms are listed in the details of the line. A `?`
there is an index name that `lists.mdl` does not declare.

**Kind** is how the variable gets its value:

| Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|
| endogenous | an equation defines it |
| exogenous | declared in `exogenous.mdl` |
| calibrated | given a value by `:=` in an equation file |
| undeclared | only met inside equations: neither defined nor declared |

**Model** is *basic model* when the variable is met in the files listed in
`config_input_threeme.R`, *other files* when it only appears in the optional
blocks (`Exception_*.mdl`).

## Counts

::: {.panel-tabset}

### By kind

```{r}
#| label: by-kind
counts <- as.data.frame.matrix(table(survey$kind, survey$model))
counts <- cbind(Kind = rownames(counts), counts, Total = rowSums(counts))
knitr::kable(counts, row.names = FALSE)
```

### By index

```{r}
#| label: by-index
by_index <- as.data.frame(sort(table(survey$index), decreasing = TRUE), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(by_index) <- c("Index", "Variables")
knitr::kable(by_index)
```

### By file

```{r}
#| label: by-file
files <- strsplit(survey$files, "; ", fixed = TRUE)
by_file <- as.data.frame(sort(table(unlist(files)), decreasing = TRUE), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(by_file) <- c("File", "Variables")
knitr::kable(by_file)
```

:::

## Still to label

The variables of the basic model with no label at all: their equation has no
`##!` line, or nothing defines or declares them.

```{r}
#| label: to-label
#| column: screen-inset
variables_table(survey[survey$core & is.na(survey$label_long_en), ], "to-label")
```
